left.title: VAR Room Operators Spotted Weeping Into Headsets After Morocco Decision
left.snippet: Sources confirm three officials requested immediate stress leave following a 47-minute video review that ultimately reversed a perfectly good goal for the fourth time this tournament...
left.author: Roberto Finch
left.content:
The Video Assistant Referee room beneath SoFi Stadium has become ground zero for what sports psychologists are calling 'a crisis of technological confidence.'

Three senior VAR operators formally requested stress leave on Wednesday after a 47-minute review process overturned a Morocco goal that even the defending goalkeeper admitted had clearly crossed the line. 'The pixel said no,' one operator reportedly whispered before being led out by colleagues.

left.title: Argentina Superfan Who Predicted Every Score Confesses He Just Guesses
left.snippet: The Buenos Aires oracle whose viral bracket has been 100% accurate through 48 matches has admitted his method involves a dartboard, a blindfold, and three cups of maté...
left.author: Lucia Montoya
left.content:
Diego Ramírez, 54, became an internet sensation when his World Cup bracket predicted every result through the group stage and Round of 16 with perfect accuracy.

'I throw a dart at a wall of team logos,' he told reporters gathered outside his apartment. 'The maté relaxes my shoulder. That is the full system.' Statisticians estimate the odds of his streak at 1 in 47 trillion. His bracket has Argentina winning on penalties.

main.title: QUARTER-FINAL RESULTS: Spain Survives Penalty Thriller; Brazil & England Crash Out in Stunning Upsets
main.snippet: NEW YORK / LOS ANGELES — The 2026 FIFA World Cup quarter-finals delivered the most chaotic 72-hour stretch in tournament history. Brazil fell to Morocco on penalties. England were eliminated by the Netherlands in extra time. Spain edged Germany 4-3 in what FIFA has already declared the match of the century. France and Argentina march on.
main.author: Chief Sports Correspondent Marco Vidal
main.content:
NEW YORK / LOS ANGELES — The 2026 FIFA World Cup quarter-finals have delivered their verdict, and the football world is in collective shock. Two of the sport's most storied nations — Brazil and England — have packed their bags and booked early flights home, while the remaining four contenders set their sights on a semi-final slate that could rewrite football history.

Netherlands 🇳🇱 vs 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England3 – 2 (AET)Levi's Stadium, SFVan Dijk bicycle kick (117')

Spain 4–3 Germany: The Match of the Century

MetLife Stadium fell into total delirium on Thursday night as Lamine Yamal, 18, scored three times in 90 minutes to dismantle Germany's resolute defensive structure. Germany equalised twice through Wirtz free-kicks before Yamal's curling effort in the 103rd minute sealed an extraordinary Spanish victory. Both managers needed oxygen at full time.


Brazil Exit: A Nation Mourns

France held their nerve across a gruelling penalty shootout after 120 minutes of football that produced just one goal apiece. Brazil's Vinicius Júnior, who missed the decisive spot kick, was inconsolable. French goalkeeper Mike Maignan saved three penalties, prompting conspiracy theories on Brazilian social media that the goalposts had been narrowed.


Messi's Farewell Goal

In what is widely expected to be his final World Cup match, Lionel Messi entered as a substitute in the 72nd minute against host nation USA and scored the winning goal with his first touch in the 88th minute. The entire Dallas stadium — including USA supporters — gave him a standing ovation. "I didn't want to score," Messi said afterward, visibly moved. "But the ball disagreed."
